articles.title: Artificial light is keeping reef fish awake, and the effects may ripple across coral reefs
articles.desc: Artificial light spilling into coastal waters from cities, ports, roads and hotels is disrupting sleep in coral reef fish and is associated with changes in markers linked to brain health, according to a new study from Bar-Ilan University. The paper, published in Current Biology, shows that even low levels of nighttime illumination can significantly alter the behavior and physiology of reef fish. Fish exposed to artificial light slept less, showed more fragmented sleep, became more aggressive and fed at unusual hours, effectively behaving as if night had turned into day.

articles.title: Are asteroid-mass black holes hiding in the cosmic gamma-ray glow?
articles.desc: There are multiple ways to form black holes. The one most commonly taught in high school physics classes is that they are created from the collapse of a dying star. But there is another class of black holes, known as primordial black holes (PBHs), that could have been created immediately after the Big Bang by matter collapsing in on itself. Or that's the theory, at least. Though long theorized, we've never actually seen one of them, though scientists have suggested that they might account for the missing mass of the universe, which we otherwise describe as "dark matter."

articles.title: Investigating quantum and molecular plumbing in nanofluidics research
articles.desc: Our body contains an intricate system of tiny vessels through which blood, water and other molecules flow. When the size of the pipes shrinks to the nanoscale, where only a few molecules can fit side by side, the classical laws of physics governing the behavior of water are influenced by the atomic structure of the walls. "It's not that classical hydrodynamics breaks down, but rather that it gets mixed with the condensed matter physics of the solid walls," says Nikita Kavokine, tenure-track assistant professor and leader of the EPFL Quantum Plumbing Lab.

articles.title: Faster aptamer screening finds synthetic alternatives to antibodies in days instead of months
articles.desc: Aptamers are short DNA or RNA strands that can recognize and bind to a specific target molecule with high precision. Similar to antibodies, they can be used to detect these molecules or modulate their activity. Unlike antibodies, they are much more stable, can be produced synthetically and can be chemically modified to achieve the desired properties. As a result, they can offer capabilities that cannot be achieved with antibodies.

Dazu gehören Hausführungen und Ausstellungen, Expertengespräche und Mitmachaktionen für Groß und Klein. Heute etwa beantwortet Regierungssprecher Kornelius Fragen von Kindern und Jugendlichen. Morgen stehen dann auch Bundeskanzler Merz, Vizekanzler Klingbeil sowie Arbeitsministerin Bas und Außenminister Wadephul Rede und Antwort. ( BAYERN 2-Nachrichten 20.06.2026 11:30)

articles.title: DFB-Elf trifft am Abend auf Elfenbeinküste
articles.desc: Toronto: Die deutsche Fußball-Nationalmannschaft bestreitet am Abend ihr zweites WM-Gruppenspiel. Gegner in Kanada ist das Team der Elfenbeinküste. Anstoß ist um 22 Uhr. Das letzte Spiel gegen Curacao hatte die Mannschaft von Bundestrainer Nagelsmann vor knapp einer Woche souverän mit 7:1 gewonnen. Bei der Weltmeisterschaft ausgeschieden ist bereits die Türkei: Das Team hat sein zweites Vorrundenspiel mit 0:1 gegen Paraguay verloren und hat damit keine Chance mehr aufs Weiterkommen. ( BAYERN 2-Nachrichten 20.06.2026 13:00)

articles.title: Das Wetter in Bayern: meist sonnig bei 31 bis 37 Grad
articles.desc: Das Wetter in Bayern: Heute vielerorts sonnig, hin und wieder Quellwolken. Im Tagesverlauf sind ganz vereinzelt kräftige gewittrige Schauer möglich. Höchstwerte 31 bis 37 Grad. In der Nacht meist klar und überwiegend trocken, vereinzelt Nebel. Tiefstwerte 21 bis 14 Grad. Bis zum Dienstag ein Mix aus Sonnenschein und mal mehr, mal weniger Wolken. Dazu punktuell Schauer und unwetterartige Gewitter. Höchstwerte: 31 bis 37 Grad. ( BAYERN 2-Nachrichten 20.06.2026 12:00)
